nl_20.teaches: the number line as a counting and place-value tool: count along, find, place and estimate numbers on 0-20, 0-50, 0-100, 0-1,000, 0-10,000 and 0-1,000,000 lines, counting in 1s, 10s, 100s ... and with only some ticks labelled
nl_20.representation: a drawn number line with some ticks labelled; write the number at the arrow, or mark a number; option: scale; option: estimate on a line with only the ends marked
nl_20.why: closes Y5.B1.S9 Number line to 1,000,000 (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

mental_add_sub.name: Mental Addition and Subtraction
mental_add_sub.teaches: mental strategies for large numbers: partitioning, counting on, compensating, near multiples
mental_add_sub.representation: a strategy prompt (round and adjust) beside each calculation
mental_add_sub.why: closes Y5.B2.S1 Mental strategies (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

estimate_big_place.name: Estimate With Large Numbers (option)
estimate_big_place.teaches: rounding 5- and 6-digit numbers to the nearest 10,000 or 100,000 to estimate a sum or difference and judge whether a worked answer is reasonable
estimate_big_place.representation: B&W boxed cell: the calculation and its claimed answer in big Andika digits, two rounding boxes under the numbers (≈ ___ + ___ = ___) and a Reasonable / Not reasonable check box; key shows the rounded numbers
estimate_big_place.why: estimate_sums_diffs places stop at 1,000, so Y5 checks with 5- and 6-digit numbers are not dealt

inverse_check.name: Inverse Operations (option)
inverse_check.teaches: using the inverse to check and to find missing numbers in addition and subtraction with 5- and 6-digit numbers
inverse_check.representation: B&W boxed cell: the worked calculation in a column stack with big Andika digits, a second empty stack for the inverse, and a Correct / Fix it check box with an answer box; option: a missing number with a bar model

vis_bar_family.teaches: the bar-model template in full: part-whole (numbers, fractions, letters, degrees), comparison (difference arrow; sum-and-difference brace; two unknowns), equal parts with `fill: 'counters' | 'disks' | 'numbers'` and `task: 'part' | 'whole'`, scaling (1 box vs n boxes) and ratio rows (a : b, a : b : c), nested / halving stacks with link arrows, unit-conversion bars (1 m cells over 100 cm), the percentage bar ("100 %" over 2–20 cells; two levels) and the journey line; offered as `model: 'bar'` on the operations hosts, and used by the fractions, algebra and measurement entries that name bar-model

compare_calcs.name: Compare Calculations
compare_calcs.teaches: comparing two calculations without working them out (4,580 + 2,000 vs 4,580 + 1,999)
compare_calcs.representation: two expressions with a circle between them; write <, > or =; reasoning prompt
compare_calcs.why: closes Y5.B2.S7 Compare calculations (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

common_mf.name: Common Multiples and Common Factors (option)
common_mf.teaches: listing multiples and factors of two numbers and circling those they share (all of them, not only the least or greatest)
common_mf.representation: two lists side by side or a Venn diagram; circle the common ones
common_mf.why: closes Y5.B3.S2 Common multiples; Y5.B3.S4 Common factors (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

square_cube.name: Square and Cube Numbers
square_cube.teaches: square numbers as square arrays and cube numbers as cubes, with the notation 5² and 2³
square_cube.representation: dot arrays and cube drawings; write the number and the notation; option: is it square?
square_cube.why: closes Y5.B3.S6 Square numbers; Y5.B3.S7 Cube numbers (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

mult_multiples.name: Multiples of 10, 100 and 1,000 (option)
mult_multiples.teaches: recognising and generating multiples of 10, 100 and 1,000

mult_multiples.why: closes Y5.B3.S10 Multiples of 10, 100 and 1,000 (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

mult_4x1.option: size "4-digit × 1-digit" (tiles 41) on the column method and the area model
mult_4x1.name: Multiply a 4-Digit Number by a 1-Digit Number (option)
mult_4x1.teaches: multiplying a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number, with the area model and the column method side by side
problemTypes: match the model to the column
mult_4x1.answer: write the product in the grid
mult_4x1.ladder: O2 no carry → carries → zero digits (3,045 × 6) · O3 carry boxes and partial products → none · O6 area model / column
misconceptions: forgets a carry into the thousands
mult_4x1.representation: area model with four parts; column method with carries; match the model to the column; estimate first
mult_4x1.why: closes Y5.B5.S1 Multiply up to a 4-digit number by a 1-digit number (existing std_props entry, reused)

long_mult.name: Long Multiplication and Division (4-digit)
long_mult.teaches: long multiplication of a 4-digit by a 2-digit number, short division of a 4-digit number, and choosing an efficient division method
long_mult.representation: a column grid with carry boxes and the placeholder row; option: short division bus stop with exchange boxes
long_mult.extendNote: for Y5.B5.S4 it must also deal 3-digit × 2-digit long multiplication (not only 4-digit × 2-digit)
long_mult.why: closes Y5.B5.S4 Multiply a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number; Y5.B5.S5 Multiply a 4-digit number by a 2-digit number; Y5.B5.S10 Efficient division (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

mult_wp_multidigit.name: Multiplication Problems With Larger Numbers (option)
mult_wp_multidigit.teaches: one- and two-step multiplication and division stories whose calculation is 4-digit × 1-digit, 2-digit × 2-digit or 4-digit ÷ 1-digit
mult_wp_multidigit.representation: B&W boxed cell: a two-line story, a bar model or equal-groups bar with the numbers in big Andika digits, a write-on calculation space and one answer box with its unit label
mult_wp_multidigit.why: every × / ÷ story skill deals table facts only, so Y5 problems with multi-digit calculations are never produced

multi_step_four_ops.option: two steps with × and ÷ (3 packs of 6, 4 eaten), write the equation with a letter for the unknown, remainder steps, and a "reasonable?" estimate
multi_step_four_ops.name: Two-Step Problems With All Four Operations (option)
multi_step_four_ops.teaches: two-step and multistep word problems with the four operations, represented by an equation with a letter, remainders interpreted, and checked by estimating
multi_step_four_ops.answer: write each step answer; write the equation
multi_step_four_ops.ladder: O2 within 100 → 1,000; two steps → three · O3 bar model and step boxes → step boxes → none · O6 pictures / plain
misconceptions: uses the letter as a label, not a number
multi_step_four_ops.extendNote: extend its number ladder (within 100 -> 1,000) on to 1,000,000 for Y5.B2.S6 (4- to 6-digit +/- two-step stories)
multi_step_four_ops.representation: × then −; ÷ then +; write the equation with n; remainder decides the answer; is the answer reasonable? (round)
multi_step_four_ops.why: closes Y5.B2.S6 Multi-step addition and subtraction problems; Y5.B5.S6 Solve problems with multiplication; Y5.B5.S11 Solve problems with multiplication and division (existing std_props entry, reused)

vis_division_layouts.name: Division Layouts: Bus Stop, Notes, Missing Digits

vis_division_layouts.teaches: the division template gains `layout: 'short'` (bus stop with small exchange-digit slots, an r slot, a decimal point and trailing zeros), `support: 'multiples'` (a multiples list beside), step notes, and `unknown` digits; box_division_* leave the legacy path
vis_division_layouts.representation: the division template gains `layout: 'short'` (bus stop with small exchange-digit slots, an r slot, a decimal point and trailing zeros), `support: 'multiples'` (a multiples list beside), step notes, and `unknown` digits; box_division_* leave the legacy path
vis_division_layouts.why: closes Y5.B5.S7 Short division (existing vis_builds entry, reused)

div_factors.name: Division Using Factors
div_factors.teaches: dividing by a 2-digit number by dividing by its factors in turn (420 ÷ 12 = 420 ÷ 2 ÷ 6)
div_factors.representation: a two-step arrow diagram with the factor pair chosen

div_factors.why: closes Y5.B5.S10 Efficient division (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

equiv_from_unit.option: start "unit fraction" (every item starts from 1/n) with a fraction-wall support
equiv_from_unit.name: Equivalent Fractions From a Unit Fraction (option)
equiv_from_unit.teaches: finding fractions equivalent to a unit fraction (1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9 = 4/12) by reading a fraction wall and by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number
equiv_from_unit.representation: one boxed cell per item: a black-outline fraction wall row for 1/n above, a second row split into smaller equal parts; write the missing numerator or denominator in a box (1/3 = __/12); Andika, big digits; the wall fades to none
equiv_from_unit.why: equivalent / equiv_frac_visual mix unit and non-unit starts, so the WRM unit-fraction lesson cannot be printed on its own

improper_direction.name: Improper ↔ Mixed: One Direction (option)
improper_direction.teaches: converting improper fractions to mixed numbers (14/4 = 3 2/4) on one page, and mixed numbers to improper fractions (3 2/4 = 14/4) on another
improper_direction.representation: boxed cell: the fraction with a bar model of wholes drawn as full bars; answer in a mixed-number slot (whole box + fraction boxes) or a fraction slot; the bars fade to none
improper_direction.why: WRM teaches the two directions as two steps (Y5.B4.S4, S5); improper_mixed always mixes them

frac_compare_gt1.name: Compare and Order Fractions Greater Than 1 (option)
frac_compare_gt1.teaches: comparing and ordering improper fractions and mixed numbers
frac_compare_gt1.representation: a band option on compare / order_fractions

frac_total_band.name: Add Fractions: Total Within 1 or Greater Than 1 (option)
frac_total_band.teaches: adding fractions with related denominators where the total stays within 1 (1/4 + 3/8 = 5/8), then where it passes 1 and is renamed as a mixed number
frac_total_band.representation: boxed cell: the sum with a bar model in eighths (black outline, one grey for shaded parts); write the numerator in the answer box; a second box for the mixed number on the >1 band
frac_total_band.why: WRM splits within-1 and over-1 into two steps; today the sums are mixed

mixed_plus_frac.option: form "mixed number ± fraction" (no exchange / crossing a whole)
mixed_plus_frac.name: Add or Subtract a Fraction and a Mixed Number (option)
mixed_plus_frac.teaches: adding a proper fraction to a mixed number (2 1/4 + 3/8) and subtracting a proper fraction from a mixed number (3 4/5 − 2/5), first without, then with crossing a whole
mixed_plus_frac.representation: boxed cell: wholes drawn as full bars and the fraction part as a partitioned bar; write the whole and the fraction in a mixed-number answer slot (two boxes)
mixed_plus_frac.why: every mixed-number skill deals mixed ± mixed; WRM Y5.B4.S12/S15/S16 start from mixed ± fraction

frac_whole_minuend.name: Subtract a Fraction From a Whole or an Improper Fraction (option)
frac_whole_minuend.teaches: subtracting a fraction from a whole number (2 − 3/4 = 1 1/4) and from an improper fraction with related denominators (7/4 − 1/2 = 5/4)
frac_whole_minuend.representation: boxed cell: the whole(s) drawn as bars split into the denominator, the parts taken away crossed out; write the answer in a fraction or mixed-number slot
frac_whole_minuend.why: WRM Y5.B4.S14 subtracts from wholes and improper fractions; every dealt item stays within 1

sub_break_whole.name: Subtract from a Mixed Number: Break the Whole (option)
sub_break_whole.teaches: subtracting a fraction larger than the fractional part of a mixed number by exchanging one whole (3 1/5 − 4/5)
sub_break_whole.representation: an "exchange a whole" band with a bar-model support

mult_unit_frac_int.option: fractions "unit only" with a repeated-addition bar
mult_unit_frac_int.name: Unit Fraction × Integer (option)
mult_unit_frac_int.teaches: multiplying a unit fraction by a whole number as repeated addition (1/5 × 3 = 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 = 3/5)

mult_unit_frac_int.why: mult_frac_whole mixes unit and non-unit fractions, so the first WRM step cannot be isolated

mult_mixed_int.name: Multiply a Mixed Number by an Integer (option)
mult_mixed_int.teaches: multiplying a mixed number by a whole number (2 1/3 × 4)

mult_mixed_int.why: no skill multiplies a mixed number by an integer; mult_frac_whole deals proper and improper fractions only (checked)

frac_find_whole.name: Fraction of an Amount: Find the Whole (option)
frac_find_whole.teaches: finding the whole from a known fractional part with a bar model (3/5 is 24, what is the whole?)

frac_operator.name: Fractions as Operators
frac_operator.teaches: using a fraction as an operator (2/5 of 30 = 30 ÷ 5 × 2) and seeing that 1/4 of 20 = 20 ÷ 4 = 20 × 1/4
frac_operator.representation: a bar model with the operator arrows; write the calculation both ways

decimal_pv.name: Tenths and Hundredths in a Place-Value Chart

thousandths_pv.name: Thousandths (option)
thousandths_pv.teaches: thousandths as fractions and decimals and on a place-value chart

dec_dp_match.option: decimal places "same" / "different" (place-holder zero shown in the column); on compare/order also "same whole part"

round_whole.name: Round Decimals to the Nearest Whole (option)
round_whole.teaches: rounding a 1-dp or 2-dp decimal to the nearest whole number on a number line
round_whole.representation: a "nearest whole" target option with a number-line support

dec_known_facts.name: Decimals from Known Facts
dec_known_facts.teaches: adding and subtracting decimals within 1 using known facts (3 + 4 = 7 so 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7), complements to 1 and efficient strategies

dec_across_one.option: items "within 1" / "across 1" with a number-line or place-value-counter support
dec_across_one.name: Add and Subtract Decimals Across 1 (option)
dec_across_one.teaches: adding and subtracting tenths and hundredths that bridge 1 (0.8 + 0.5 = 1.3; 1.2 − 0.4 = 0.8), first by bridging through 1 on a number line, then in the column
dec_across_one.representation: boxed cell: a 0–2 number line in tenths with the jump to 1 drawn, then the equation with an answer box; the line fades to none
dec_across_one.why: decimal_models adds pictures but no across-1 item control; add_decimal crosses 1 only at random

decimal_models.option: support "decimal model": hundred squares or place-value counters beside the column, and an area model for decimal × whole

decimal_models.teaches: adding, subtracting and multiplying decimals to hundredths with a drawn model that is related to the written method
problemTypes: add with hundred squares, then the column
subtract with an exchange of a tenth
multiply a decimal by a whole with an area model
decimal_models.answer: write the answer in the column (the model is support)
decimal_models.ladder: O2 tenths → hundredths → crossing 1 · O3 model with exchanges drawn → model only → none · O6 hundred squares / counters
misconceptions: lines up the right-hand digits, not the points

dec_sequence.name: Decimal Sequences
dec_sequence.teaches: continuing and finding the rule of sequences with decimal steps (0.2, 0.4, 0.6 ... ; 1.5, 1.25, 1.0)
dec_sequence.representation: a number track with decimal steps; write the missing terms and the rule

dec_missing.name: Multiply and Divide Decimals: Missing Values (option)
dec_missing.teaches: finding the missing number or the missing power of 10 (3.4 × __ = 340)

frac_beyond_1.name: Fractions Beyond 1
frac_beyond_1.teaches: counting beyond 1 in fractions, partitioning a mixed number into wholes and a fraction, mixed numbers on a number line
frac_beyond_1.representation: bar and number-line models with wholes shaded; write the mixed number

decimal_whole.name: Make a Whole with Decimals
decimal_whole.teaches: complements to 1 with tenths and hundredths (0.3 + 0.7, 0.45 + 0.55)
decimal_whole.representation: a tenths strip or hundred square with part shaded; write the missing part

missing_lengths.name: Missing Lengths in Rectilinear Shapes
missing_lengths.teaches: finding missing side lengths in rectilinear shapes and then their perimeter

regular_polygon.name: Perimeter of Regular Polygons (option)

regular_polygon.why: closes Y5.B8.S3 Perimeter of polygons (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

area_estimate.name: Estimate Area
area_estimate.teaches: estimating the area of irregular shapes by counting whole and half squares
area_estimate.representation: an irregular blob on squared paper; count whole and part squares; write the estimate
area_estimate.why: closes Y5.B8.S6 Estimate area (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

line_graph.name: Line Graphs
line_graph.teaches: reading and drawing line graphs that show change over time

table_data.name: Tables

two_way.name: Two-Way Tables
two_way.representation: a two-way table with blanks and totals; fill them in
two_way.why: closes Y5.B9.S4 Two-way tables (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

timetables.name: Timetables
timetables.teaches: reading and calculating with bus and train timetables (times, durations, which bus)
timetables.representation: a drawn timetable table; answer questions with times and durations
timetables.why: closes Y5.B14.S6 Calculate with timetables; Y5.B9.S5 Read and interpret timetables (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

turns_angles.name: Turns and Angles
turns_angles.teaches: an angle as an amount of turn; right angles as quarter turns; comparing angles with a right angle (greater/less)

turns_angles.why: closes Y5.B10.S1 Understand and use degrees (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

reflex_angles.name: Reflex Angles (option)
reflex_angles.teaches: naming reflex angles (more than 180°, less than 360°) beside acute, right, obtuse and straight

angle_estimate.option: form "estimate": acute/obtuse first, then write an estimate in degrees (accept ±15°)

protractor_read.option: form "read the protractor": a protractor drawn over the angle; write the degrees (not multiple choice)

draw_angles.name: Draw Angles and Lines

draw_angles.why: closes Y5.B10.S5 Draw lines and angles accurately (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

ruler_cm.name: Read a Centimetre Ruler (option)

angles_point.name: Angles Around a Point and on a Line (option)

lengths_angles_shapes.name: Lengths and Angles in Shapes
lengths_angles_shapes.teaches: using properties of rectangles, squares and regular polygons to find missing lengths and angles

polygons.name: Regular and Irregular Polygons

shapes_3d_props.name: 3-D Shapes: Names and Properties
shapes_3d_props.teaches: naming 3-D shapes (prisms, pyramids) from faces, edges and vertices and from their 2-D views or nets

shapes_3d_props.why: closes Y5.B10.S10 3-D shapes (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

coord_missing_vertex.option: task "missing vertex": three vertices of a rectangle or square given; write the fourth
coord_missing_vertex.name: Find the Missing Vertex (option)
coord_missing_vertex.teaches: using equal sides and right angles to find a missing vertex on a first-quadrant grid
coord_missing_vertex.representation: a B&W coordinate grid with three plotted, labelled vertices and dashed sides; write ( , ) in boxes
coord_missing_vertex.why: coord_polygon only measures sides; WRM Y5 problem solving is the missing vertex

translate_grid.name: Translate on a Grid
translate_grid.teaches: translating a shape or point on a first-quadrant grid and describing a translation (3 right, 2 up)
translate_grid.representation: a coordinate grid with a shape and its image; write the translation or draw the image
translate_grid.why: closes Y5.B11.S3 Translation; Y5.B11.S4 Translation with coordinates (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

reflect_grid.name: Reflect on a Grid
reflect_grid.teaches: reflecting a shape in a horizontal or vertical mirror line on a square grid and in the axes
reflect_grid.representation: a grid with a dashed mirror line and a shape; draw the reflection; key shows it
reflect_grid.why: closes Y5.B11.S6 Reflection in horizontal and vertical lines (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

symmetry_complete.name: Complete the Symmetric Shape
symmetry_complete.teaches: using a vertical line of symmetry to complete a shape or pattern on a square grid
symmetry_complete.representation: half a shape on squared paper beside a dashed mirror line; draw the other half
symmetry_complete.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B11.S6 (existing entry, reused)

negative_count.name: Count Through Zero
negative_count.teaches: negative numbers in context (temperature), counting through zero in 1s and multiples, and the difference between a positive and a negative number
negative_count.representation: a vertical thermometer or number line; write the next numbers or the difference
negative_count.why: closes Y5.B13.S1 Understand negative numbers; Y5.B13.S2 Count through zero in 1s; Y5.B13.S3 Count through zero in multiples; Y5.B13.S5 Find the difference (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

km_m.name: Kilometres and Metres (option)
km_m.teaches: measuring and converting km and m, including mixed units (2 km 300 m)
km_m.extendNote: For Y5.B14.S1/S3 it must also convert smaller to larger (3,500 m = 3 km 500 m = 3.5 km), not only mixed units.
km_m.why: closes Y5.B14.S1 Kilograms and kilometres; Y5.B14.S3 Convert units of length (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

kg_g_convert.option: units "kg and g": both directions and mixed units
kg_g_convert.name: Kilograms and Grams (option)
kg_g_convert.teaches: 1 kg = 1,000 g: convert both ways and between mixed units (2 kg 350 g = 2,350 g)
kg_g_convert.representation: one item per boxed cell: a fact box "1 kg = 1,000 g" and a sentence with answer boxes "_ kg _ g"
kg_g_convert.why: no skill converts g→kg or mixed kg/g units

mm_cm_m.name: Metres, Centimetres, Millimetres (option)
mm_cm_m.teaches: measuring in mm, cm and m and converting between them (2 m 30 cm = 230 cm)
mm_cm_m.representation: ruler pictures in mm; mixed-unit answers (_ m _ cm)
mm_cm_m.extendNote: For Y5.B14.S2/S3 it must also convert smaller to larger (450 cm = 4 m 50 cm; 63 mm = 6 cm 3 mm), not only larger to smaller.
mm_cm_m.why: closes Y5.B14.S2 Millimetres and millilitres; Y5.B14.S3 Convert units of length (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

l_ml_convert.option: units "l and ml": both directions and mixed units
l_ml_convert.name: Litres and Millilitres (option)
l_ml_convert.teaches: 1 l = 1,000 ml both ways and with mixed units
l_ml_convert.representation: a drawn jug scale (black outline, single grey fill) and answer boxes "_ l _ ml" / "_ ml"
l_ml_convert.why: capacity converts L→mL one way only and mixes in customary units

metric_imperial.name: Metric and Imperial Units
metric_imperial.teaches: approximate conversions between metric and imperial units (1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb)
metric_imperial.representation: a conversion fact box beside each question
metric_imperial.why: closes Y5.B14.S4 Convert between metric and imperial units (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

time_convert.name: Convert Units of Time (option)
time_convert.teaches: converting between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years
time_convert.why: closes Y5.B14.S5 Convert units of time (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

capacity_estimate.option: form "estimate": choose or write a sensible capacity in ml or l
capacity_estimate.name: Estimate Capacity (option)
capacity_estimate.teaches: estimating capacity with benchmarks (teaspoon 5 ml, cup 250 ml, bottle 1 l, bucket 10 l)
capacity_estimate.representation: one black line drawing of a container per boxed cell beside a benchmark; circle one of three estimates or write it with the unit
capacity_estimate.why: capacity sorts containers but never writes an estimate in ml/l

volume_cubes.name: Volume by Counting Cubes
volume_cubes.teaches: volume as the number of unit cubes (cm³), comparing volumes and estimating volume and capacity
volume_cubes.representation: isometric drawings of cube solids; write how many cubes / cm³; option: which has more
volume_cubes.why: closes Y5.B15.S1 Cubic centimetres; Y5.B15.S2 Compare volume; Y5.B15.S3 Estimate volume (existing wrm_props entry, reused)

mass_scales.name: Read Scales (g, kg, ml, l)
mass_scales.teaches: reading mass and capacity scales in grams, kilograms, millilitres and litres with scale steps of 1, 2, 5, 10, 100
mass_scales.representation: a drawn dial or jug scale; write the reading with the unit; option: scale step
mass_scales.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B14.S1, Y5.B14.S2, Y5.B15.S4 (existing entry, reused)

roman_12.name: Roman Numerals to 12
roman_12.teaches: reading Roman numerals I to XII on a clock face
roman_12.representation: a clock face with Roman numerals; write the time or the numeral value
roman_12.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B1.S1 (existing entry, reused)

roman_100.name: Roman Numerals
roman_100.teaches: reading and writing Roman numerals to 100 (I, V, X, L, C) and knowing there is no zero
roman_100.representation: numeral cards with a symbol key; write the value or the numeral
roman_100.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B1.S1 (existing entry, reused)

bonds_100.name: Bonds to 100
bonds_100.teaches: pairs of tens that make 100 (30 + 70) and later any pair (37 + 63), from bonds to 10
bonds_100.representation: a hundred square or bead string with part shaded; part-whole diagram; write the missing part
bonds_100.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B2.S1 (existing entry, reused)

mult_three.name: Multiply Three Numbers
mult_three.teaches: multiplying three 1-digit numbers using the associative property (2 × 5 × 7 = 10 × 7)
mult_three.representation: three-factor expressions with a bracket prompt to choose the easy pair first
mult_three.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B3.S7 (existing entry, reused)

correspondence.name: Correspondence Problems
correspondence.teaches: one-to-many correspondence (each of 3 hats with each of 4 scarves; 1 bag holds 5) as multiplication
correspondence.representation: a table or tree diagram to complete, then the multiplication
correspondence.why: needed as a pre-skill for Y5.B5.S6, Y5.B5.S11 (existing entry, reused)
